# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles WGS84 coordinates, indigenous and archaeological names, occupation spans and benchmark population series for 195 pre-contact settlements across Northern Cascadia and Alaska (`2,80M km²`) from `10000BC` to `1600AD`. Excavated winter villages, shell-midden towns and stratified pit-house aggregates range from `10000BC` Beringian hearths at Swan Point (`150` peak) and Broken Mammoth (`55`) and the `8500BC` coastal midden at Namu (`540` peak) to late Holocene plank-house and pit-house towns at Marpole (`1,45k`), Keatley Creek (`1,4k`), Yuquot (`1,2k`), Laxgalts'ap (`920`), Bridge River (`820`), Karluk (`820`), Gitwangak (`720`), Sitka (`680`), Victoria (`620`) and Utqiagvik (`620`). Every included site carries CENTAUR provenance in the settlement gazetteer and reconciles cleanly against `196` source-ledger candidates alongside 1 consolidated duplicate-alias record.

# Background

Settlement archaeology across Alaska, Yukon and British Columbia distinguishes three major residential traditions [@ames1999; @matson1995]. Along the Salish Sea, Vancouver Island, Haida Gwaii and Skeena-Nass fjords, multi-lineage red-cedar plank-house towns sat atop deep coastal shell middens and commanded fortified ridge refuges such as Gitwangak and Boardwalk [@macdonald1989; @martindale2009]. Across the Fraser-Columbia Plateau and the Aleutian-Kodiak littoral, semi-subterranean earth-roofed pit houses clustered in winter villages such as Keatley Creek, Bridge River, Karluk and Chaluka [@hayden1997; @fitzhugh2003; @laughlin1980]. On the Bering, Chukchi and Beaufort coasts, whalebone-and-sod winter mounds at Utqiagvik, Gambell, Wales and Cape Krusenstern housed Arctic marine-mammal hunters [@larsen1948; @giddings1986].

# Methodology

Candidate entries in the source ledger qualify for inclusion when excavation monographs, regional radiocarbon syntheses or heritage inventories supply bounded geographic coordinates, dated cultural horizons and house-floor or site-area demographic estimates [@maples2006; @martindale2009]. Overlapping coordinate twins within `2 km` are consolidated as duplicate aliases so each locality contributes once to settlement subtraction. Table \ref{tab:summary} summarises included site counts and summed site peaks across the five sub-regions.

# Testing and Validation

Exhaustiveness checks between the `195` catalogued settlements and the `196` ledger candidates pass with `0` unaccounted entries (`195` included, `1` consolidated duplicate alias) and `0` schema faults. All WGS84 coordinates fall within valid regional bounds (`48,46` to `71,29` N and `117,52` to `176,63` W), every record carries CENTAUR provenance and Figure \ref{fig:settlements} charts the rank-size hierarchy across the `195` catalogued settlements.

## Sub-Regional Settlement Summaries

Across the Salish Sea, Vancouver Island and Fraser-Columbia Plateau (`46` settlements), coastal shell-midden occupation begins at Namu (`540` peak, occupied from `8500BC` to `1500AD`) [@carlson1996] and culminates in large plank-house and pit-house towns at Marpole (`1,45k` peak), Keatley Creek (`1,4k` in `1000AD`), Yuquot (`1,2k`), Bridge River (`820`), Victoria (`620`), Tsawwassen (`580`) and Bell Site (`520`) [@hayden1997; @dewar2001; @samuels1991]. On the Inside Passage, Haida Gwaii and Skeena-Nass coast (`51` settlements), Laxgalts'ap (`920` peak), Gitwangak (`720`), Sitka (`680`), Lax Kw'alaams (`610`), Massett (`580`), Boardwalk (`560`) and Bella Coola (`540`) anchor outer-fjord Tlingit, Haida and Tsimshian exchange [@macdonald1989; @martindale2009]. Farther north along the Aleutian-Kodiak littoral (`25` settlements), Karluk (`820`), Izembek (`540`) and Chaluka (`520`) document dense maritime villages [@laughlin1980; @fitzhugh2003], while Utqiagvik (`620`), Gambell (`580`), Wales (`520`), Kukulik (`520`) and Cape Krusenstern (`480`) lead the `43` Arctic Alaska whaling hubs [@larsen1948; @giddings1986]. Interior Yukon-Tanana (`30` settlements) retains lower-density riverine and lakeside loci led by Pauline Cove (`390` peak), Yakutat (`360`), Klondike-Tr'ochëk (`220`), Swan Point (`150` from `10000BC`), Healy Lake (`95`) and Bluefish Caves (`20`) [@holmes2001; @morlan2003; @cook1996].

# Limitations

Gazetteer visibility remains skewed toward deep coastal shell middens, outer-fjord cedar plank-house villages and stratified Fraser canyon pit-house aggregates over dispersed boreal hunting camps. Post-glacial sea-level rise along Hecate Strait and coseismic subsidence in south-central Alaska submerged early coastal shorelines prior to `5000BC`, leaving mobile and submerged populations represented primarily within the rural kriging surface.
